Geauga Lake, Abandoned Amusement Park - Drone Flyover

Cleveland.com posted this video yesterday evening, and while I agree with it's lone YouTube comment that it's a little short, I still found it interesting (and unseen) enough to pass along here.

Someone in the cleveland.com comment section also shared a link to a reasonably in depth story about the rise and fall of Geauga Lake that put the abrupt end of the amusement park in better perspective for me. I guess most people always looked at it as the 'little brother' of Cedar Point, but if you grew up/lived in the area chances are you were always aware of both. It's sad (if not unsurprising) to see how quickly the remains of the park deteriorated.

I've had a fascination with abandoned amusement parks for a long time. I live near the Rocky River Metroparks and a long dead amusement park, Puritas Springs, can still be seen in the dry winter months up by the edge of Puritas Ave.

http://www.westparkhistory.com/articles/PuritasSprings/PuritasSprings.htm

My grandparents also owned a cottage next to Chippewa Lake amusement park back in the 60s. My dad was a lifeguard there for many years. I've made many trips down there just to see the old coaster, ferris wheel, and bandstand.

http://www.forgottenoh.com/Chippewa/chippewa.html

It's too bad about Geauga Lake. Six Flags just bit off more than they could chew. I have fond memories of the park as well as Seaworld which was next door.

This is the first time I've heard of Puritas Springs, so I really appreciate that link, thank you! Next time I see my family I'm definitely going to ask them if they know anything about the place. Looks like it closed down a little before my parents' time, but they've spoken numerous times about Euclid Beach Park, which was closer to where they grew up and closed about a decade later. They're certainly much more aware of Cleveland history than I am, and knew lots of people plenty older than them, so you never know.

Small, local amusement parks are kind of a lost art I guess. It's hard to compete when you've got a place like Cedar Point constantly growing and within driving distance...

Same as you, I was at both Seaworld and Geauga Lake a few times each growing up, and also have fond memories of those visits. Sort of felt like it lost its charm after Six Flags got involved and plastered Batman and Bugs Bunny all over everything, though I never thought too deeply about it. Then, in its final years when Cedar Fair took over, I went there one last time with some friends and the place felt kinda rough... you could see the writing on the wall.
